source_snapshot.procedure: Check the test-item information, collect evidence, reboot and verify it remains correct.
source_snapshot.criteria: Information is correct and remains correct after reboot.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek runs dmidecode Type 2 then grep around Product Name, but calls filtered text full raw output, provides no approved expected value and does not perform the required reboot/re-read.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify that the SMBIOS Type 2 Baseboard Product Name for every owner-applicable baseboard record equals the platform-approved identity and remains identical after reboot.
original_test_intent.target: The applicable SMBIOS Type 2 Baseboard Information structure(s) on the exact SUT, mapped by structure handle plus companion manufacturer/serial/asset/location/chassis/baseboard-type data when multiple Type 2 records exist; not the Type 1 System Product Name.
original_test_intent.scope: Read and compare the Type 2 Product Name before and after one approved reboot, preserving the complete structures and stable mapping for all required baseboards.
original_test_intent.operation: Record SUT/firmware/SMBIOS and expected baseboard identity, collect unfiltered Type 2 structures with validated dmidecode, map each applicable record, compare Product Name with the owner recipe, obtain reboot approval, reboot, repeat the same collection and mapping, and compare value and persistence plus boot/management health.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: Two read-only captures separated by one approved reboot; no additional loop is specified.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Each required Type 2 record is present and unambiguously mapped; its Product Name exactly matches the approved value before reboot and is unchanged/correct afterward; the SUT and management path return healthy.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/board/BIOS/BMC and SMBIOS version identity, dmidecode version, expected per-baseboard Product Name matrix, complete raw pre/post Type 2 output with handles and companion fields, parser result, reboot timeline, byte/string comparison, and host/OOB health.
ambiguities: The source gives no expected Product Name or mapping when more than one Type 2 structure is present.
It does not define case/whitespace/placeholder handling or whether every baseboard record must be checked.
The procedure omits the explicit reboot action even though the criterion requires post-reboot persistence.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly distinguishes Type 2 from Type 1, requires a supplied expected value, complete output, reboot approval and pre/post comparison. It assumes a singular baseboard and does not define how to map and verify multiple Type 2 structures, a valid server possibility.

applicable_history.decision: The historical review accepts a direct dmidecode path but delegates correctness/persistence judgment and does not resolve expected value or multi-record mapping.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Retain the hybrid classification because collection/comparison are automatable but expected identity and reboot require owner input/approval. V3 adds per-handle mapping for multiple Type 2 records and rejects grep-only evidence as complete output.

available_now: The intended SMBIOS structure and field are exact: Type 2 Baseboard Product Name.
Pre-reboot Type 2 data can be collected read-only even before the expected value is supplied.
DMTF defines Type 2 as Baseboard Information, while dmidecode explicitly reports firmware-provided SMBIOS data and warns it should not be blindly trusted as hardware discovery.
missing_inputs: Approved Product Name for every applicable baseboard and mapping by board role/handle/companion identity
Comparison normalization policy for trailing spaces, empty/default/placeholder strings and duplicate records
Validated dmidecode package/sudo access, authenticated host path, approved reboot window, workload quiescence and OOB recovery
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The platform/firmware owner supplies the expected per-baseboard identity and comparison policy; the lab/system owner supplies validated tooling/access, approves the reboot and provides OOB recovery.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect `dmidecode --version`, SMBIOS version and complete `dmidecode -t 2` output with all handles/fields; also retain board/firmware/SUT identity without clearing logs
Build a provisional table of every Type 2 handle, Manufacturer, Product Name, Version, Serial, Asset Tag, Location, Chassis Handle and Board Type, marking acceptance pending
prohibited_until_closed: Do not declare PASS from presence/non-empty text, grep a single first match, confuse Type 1 and Type 2, drop extra Type 2 records or treat dmidecode as independent physical-board proof
Do not reboot without approval/workload isolation/OOB recovery, modify firmware/SMBIOS, clear logs or normalize mismatches without an owner rule
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner matrix maps every required Type 2 handle/role to one exact Product Name and normalization rule; dmidecode/access are validated; pre-reboot output is complete; reboot and recovery are approved; the same record mapping can be reproduced post-reboot.

revision_candidate.test_name: SMBIOS Type 2 Baseboard Product Name Persistence
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify the Product Name of every applicable SMBIOS Type 2 Baseboard record against the approved platform identity before and after one reboot.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact server/board/BIOS build with an owner-approved per-baseboard identity matrix, Linux access to validated dmidecode, an approved reboot window and working console/BMC/OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: All owner-required SMBIOS Type 2 structures. Map each by structure handle and companion baseboard identity/role; exclude Type 1 System Information and do not silently choose the first Product Name.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Expected Product Name per baseboard/role; structure mapping and comparison-normalization rule; dmidecode version/package and sudo access; SUT credentials; workload/reboot approval; stable power, OOB recovery and evidence destination.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Capture SUT/SMBIOS/tool identity and complete raw Type 2 output; map all applicable handles and compare their Product Names with the signed matrix; after explicit approval reboot once; repeat identical collection/mapping; compare correctness and persistence and verify host/BMC health.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Exact SUT and expected matrix selected; all Type 2 roles resolvable; dmidecode validated; authenticated least-privilege access available; workload quiesced; reboot window, power and OOB recovery ready; pre-existing logs preserved.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Signed per-handle/role expected matrix; dmidecode/SMBIOS versions; unfiltered pre/post Type 2 records and hashes; extracted companion fields/Product Names; exact comparison results; reboot start/return timeline; host/OS/BMC health and exception record.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact platform/baseboard product-identity specification for this SUT plus DMTF SMBIOS Type 2 field semantics; DMTF defines the field location, not the vendor-specific expected string.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Use read-only SMBIOS collection only; never write firmware data, clear logs, accept the wrong structure, discard duplicate records, reboot without approval or infer physical identity solely from firmware-reported strings.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Platform owner approves the expected identity/mapping and resolves discrepancies; system/workload owner approves reboot. No approval is needed for ordinary pre-reboot read-only collection.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owner supplies/accepts identity and authorizes reboot. Once inputs are machine-readable, collection, structure parsing, comparison, reboot orchestration within approval and health checks can be automated.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: If reboot, host or management recovery fails, stop and use approved console/BMC/OOB recovery. On identity drift or ambiguity, preserve both complete dumps and firmware context; do not flash or rewrite SMBIOS under this case.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Missing expected mapping, unresolved multiple Type 2 records, invalid/incomplete dump, ambiguous/placeholder Product Name, pre-test mismatch, absent reboot approval/recovery, boot/management failure, post-reboot record drift or incomplete evidence.

identified_defects: DeepSeek's grep output is neither complete raw evidence nor a post-reboot persistence test.
V2 does not explicitly cover multiple Type 2 Baseboard structures or map them by handle/role.
The source lacks the vendor-specific expected value and comparison policy; DMTF semantics alone cannot establish correctness.
reason_for_change: Prevent a server with multiple baseboard structures from passing on one arbitrary Product Name and make the required reboot persistence comparison complete and reproducible.

new_technical_evidence.title: DMTF DSP0134 SMBIOS Specification
new_technical_evidence.version: 3.8.0; current platform-supported SMBIOS version must be recorded
new_technical_evidence.applicability: SMBIOS Type 2 structures exposed by the SUT firmware
new_technical_evidence.supports: Type 2 is Baseboard Information and has companion baseboard attributes used to disambiguate board records; the standard defines representation but not the ODM's required Product Name string.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The SUT-specific expected name and applicable record mapping are not public in the source.

new_technical_evidence.title: dmidecode project documentation
new_technical_evidence.version: project documentation accessed 2026-10-13; installed version must be recorded
new_technical_evidence.supports: dmidecode reports SMBIOS/DMI data supplied by system firmware and warns that DMI data must not be blindly trusted as independent hardware detection.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The qualified package/version and privilege model are environment-specific.

removed_ambiguities: Defines all applicable Type 2 records and the companion fields needed for stable mapping.
Separates standard field semantics from the owner-specific expected value.
Makes the source criterion's reboot a required explicit phase.
resolved_blockers: Missing expected value does not prevent safe collection of actual Type 2 data; it blocks PASS comparison only.
remaining_blockers: PASS and reboot remain blocked until per-record expected identity/mapping, normalization policy, tooling/access, approval and recovery are ready.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 extends V2's correct Type 2 and reboot controls to multi-baseboard servers, retains complete per-handle records instead of grep-only text, and clearly separates DMTF structure semantics from vendor identity acceptance.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The isolated validator preserved every applicable SMBIOS Type 2 record, unique baseboard-role mapping and exact Product Name comparison before and after one reboot.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The case checks SMBIOS Type 2 Baseboard Product Name correctness and requires the information to remain correct after reboot.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 supplies the missing reboot and Type 2 distinction but assumes a singular baseboard rather than mapping every applicable Type 2 record.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Collect complete firmware-reported Type 2 records read-only, compare every mapped handle to owner values, and reboot only after approval/OOB readiness; never rewrite SMBIOS on mismatch.
